description: When the sense-doors are closed with the hands, a point of light (bindu) is seen; as it gradually dissolves, the supreme state is in its midst.
A point like a subtle fiery mark arising from agitation within the light-abode, meditated at the crest or in the heart.
The unstruck sound, unbroken, rushing like a river, heard within; immersion in it leads to the supreme Brahman.
With the currents blocked and the breath-power rising slowly, a sensation like crawling ants, at which supreme joy spreads.

One established in any dhāraṇā accomplishes deeds by speech, grants curse and grace, is free of old age and death, has the powers such as aṇimā, is dear to the yoginīs and lord of their gatherings, and is liberated while living.

Bliss (ānanda), leaping up (udbhava), trembling (kampa), sleep (nidrā) and whirling (ghūrṇi) - signs of immersion observed in the initiand; applied by Abhinavagupta to the āṇava practice of the breath (TĀ 5.101-111).

Signs that Rudra's power has descended: unwavering devotion to Rudra, success in mantra with immediate confirmation, control over beings, completion of undertakings, poetic power with sudden knowledge of all scriptures.
Seven blisses recognized in the contemplation of the breath: nijānanda, nirānanda, parānanda, brahmānanda, mahānanda, cidānanda, jagadānanda.
In extreme anger, great joy, perplexity or running, the state reached is where spanda is established.
From the unmeṣa arise quickly light, sound, form and taste, agitating the embodied - read as a caution.
Resting in spanda, in- and out-breath set in the suṣumnā and rise beyond the cosmic egg; in that great space the deluded are as in deep sleep, the awakened unveiled.
For the yogin resting in spanda, desired objects are accomplished in waking and clearly revealed in dream.
Wonder (vismaya) marks the stages of yoga.
The bliss of the world is the joy of samādhi.

Production of bodies, joining and separating elements, assembling the universe, mastery of the wheel of powers; mastery of the elements (3.5) - with the warning that powers under the veil of delusion are not liberation (3.6).
Samādhi that remains in all activity; lordship over the circle of the deities of one's own consciousness.
By restraint of the breath Lal Ded lit the lamp of knowledge and saw the stainless form of consciousness.
